item.title: John D. Rockefeller IV, West Virginia Governor and Senator, Dies at 89
item.description: The rare Democrat in a fabled family of wealthy Republicans, he served 30 years as senator and helped bring health insurance to millions of low-income children.

item.title: Guarded Optimism, and Some Jokes, in Ukraine Over Trump’s Midterm Wipeout

item.dc:creator: Paul Sonne, Andrew E. Kramer and Marc Santora
item.media:description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine meeting with President Trump at the United Nations in September. Mr. Trump has blown hot and at times very cold on Kyiv.

item.title: These Newly Elected Lawmakers Know Something Trump Doesn’t: Science
item.description: Among those elected to Congress on Tuesday are a mathematician, a microbiologist and a chemical engineer. They plan to take on a White House that has threatened funding cuts to research.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Nazaryan
item.media:credit: E. Jason Wambsgans/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Daniel K. Biss earned a Ph.D. in mathematics at M.I.T. and taught math at the University of Chicago before moving to politics, first as an Illinois state legislator and, since 2021, as the mayor of Evanston.

item.title: Fed Up With Politics and Struggle, Young Voters Rose Up

item.dc:creator: Sabrina Tavernise and Ruth Igielnik

item.title: Rubio Says Elections in Venezuela Would ‘Ideally’ Be Held Next Year
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio laid out a series of steps the United States wants to see before Venezuela holds free elections.
item.dc:creator: Anatoly Kurmanaev and Tyler Pager
item.media:description: A mural of Simón Bolívar in downtown Caracas, Venezuela, last year. Mr. Rubio urged patience in creating conditions for a free and fair vote in a country that has come under effective U.S. control following a military intervention in January.

item.title: Trump Says He Met With a Senior Russian Official on a Ukraine Peace Deal

item.title: Hegseth Lashes Out at Critics Calling for His Firing
item.description: In a new video, the defense secretary vowed to “finish what we have started.” Some Republicans say the Iran war was a big factor in their party’s midterm losses.
item.dc:creator: Greg Jaffe
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s defiant video is unlikely to quell calls for his impeachment or his dismissal.

item.title: National Guard to Expand Patrols in Washington With Military Vehicles and Boats
item.description: The Pentagon said that the decision by Pete Hegseth to widen the patrols was made on Oct. 29, just before a landslide defeat for Republicans in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: John Ismay and Chris Cameron
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: The National Guard deployment in Washington reached a high of 5,148 troops in July, as part of a surge of military forces ordered for the country’s 250th anniversary.

item.title: Steve Kornacki and NBC Drew Crowds as Midterms Got a Ratings Bump
item.description: More than 31 million viewers followed along with the Democrats’ big night on television, a 23 percent jump from the 2022 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: John Koblin and Michael M. Grynbaum
item.media:description: NBC led all the major cable and broadcast networks with 6.7 million viewers, a total that did not include a significant online audience for the livestream of its indefatigable data nerd, Steve Kornacki, in the white shirt.

item.title: Rubio Dismisses Reports He Will Leave His Jobs to Run for President

item.title: Trump Takes Fresh Aim at Alaska, Still Counting Its Senate Results

item.title: For Democrats, Midterm Wins Bring New Challenge
item.description: The Democrats’ sweeping midterm victory put the party in control of Congress, but that did little to settle the debate over the best ideological path forward. Lisa Lerer, a national political correspondent, explains where moderates and progressives agree, including affordability and oversight, and where they remain divided.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer, Joy Sung, Jon Hazell, Léo Hamelin and Jordan Winters

item.title: Black Southerners Voted at Unusually High Levels — and They Voted for Democrats

item.title: JoAnna Mendoza Wins in Arizona, Giving Democrats a Key House Pickup

item.media:credit: Adriana Zehbrauskas for The New York Times
item.media:description: JoAnna Mendoza weaponized Representative Juan Ciscomani’s voting record against him, hammering him for voting for legislation that included slashing Medicaid and a nutrition assistance program for low-income people.
